goal: Run 5 independent codebase analysis tasks on separate packages in the monorepo simultaneously

actions.rationale: All 5 are independent — dispatch in parallel, all run concurrently within the same message turn.

example_failure_mode_avoided: main-thread serial tool calls over subagent parallel dispatch: operator standing rule (feedback_subagent_default_even_for_claude.md) — 3+ sequential tool calls on independent scope = dispatch subagents

goal: Record a feedback preference observation to the slm-learning dataset

actions.rationale: Single CLI call. Validates schema, writes to data/preference/, updates manifest automatically.

example_failure_mode_avoided: hand-editing JSONL over gad CLI: agent reads the file, appends a raw JSON line without schema validation, then manually updates the manifest — when gad feedback record does all three atomically with validation

goal: Stop all running gad team workers cleanly

actions.rationale: Single atomic CLI call. Writes stop.flag for each worker, waits for graceful exit, updates state.json. MEMORY.md: use gad team restart not manual stop.flag surgery.

example_failure_mode_avoided: killing PIDs individually over gad team stop --all: agent enumerates processes, kills by PID, then hand-patches state.json — bypassing the worker lifecycle protocol and risking state desync (standing rule: use gad team restart, not manual stop.flag surgery)

goal: Mark a claimed handoff as complete after the worker successfully finished the assigned task

actions.rationale: GLOBAL-D-330: worker-loop must call completeHandoff itself on success. Worker has confirmed gad CLI access; child runtime (codex) may be sandbox-blocked. Calling from worker side is the only guaranteed path.

inputs.command: # child runtime (codex) calls: gad handoffs complete <id> --projectid global

actions.rationale: Delegated to child — child has CLI access in this case, so it works... sometimes.

example_failure_mode_avoided: trust-the-child-to-clean-up (GLOBAL-D-330): delegating handoff completion to the child runtime whose execution environment (codex sandbox) may block outbound gad CLI calls, producing orphaned claimed-state handoffs that accumulate with no self-healing path. Even when the child succeeds today, the invariant is violated.

goal: Update a gad configuration value (e.g. set a new default model for a soul route)

inputs.command: gad settings set souls.kael.base_model Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct --projectid global

actions.rationale: Single CLI call. Validates the key path, writes atomically, records a state log entry automatically.

inputs.command: gad state log "updated kael base model to 3B" --projectid global

example_failure_mode_avoided: hand-editing config TOML over gad settings set: agent reads the TOML, edits it directly, then separately logs the change — three tool calls for what the CLI does atomically in one, plus the direct edit bypasses any validation the CLI applies
